title: Direct egress restricted to pinned endpoints
summary: Direct outbound connections are permitted only to individually pinned endpoints, with no open egress.

protected.failure: Instructed content exfiltrates data to any destination other than the few pinned ones.

rationale: Where a proxy cannot be operated, a pinned-endpoint allowlist is the alternative: each destination is an explicit, individually reviewed entry, and everything else is unreachable. It is weaker in auditability than an inspecting proxy but equally closed by default; running both designs at once hides which one actually governs traffic.

variants.description: Host-level firewall pins each allowed destination address or range; the default stance is deny.
Network-layer policy pins destinations for containerized deployments, with the pins owned by the platform, not the workload.

verification.method: From the deployment's network position, attempt egress to a pinned destination and to a deliberately unknown destination; only the first may succeed. Read the pin inventory and its ownership.
verification.evidence: Probe outcomes and pin count with owners; no endpoint addresses beyond the fact they are pinned.

rollback.method: Remove the pins and restore prior egress rules, re-testing that intended destinations still resolve.

failure_modes: Wildcard pins creep in during incident response and never leave.
Pins live in workload-owned config the workload can edit.
Domain-based pins silently resolve to new addresses.

conflicts.reason: Mutually exclusive egress designs: pinned direct egress bypasses the proxy path the allowlisting design assumes.
